subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw adopt RFC 0024’s shared localization runtime and fixed 22-locale product-coverage contract, including new plugin metadata and eventual release-blocking completeness gates?
rationale: The proposal intentionally crosses established surface ownership and would create durable plugin, storage, compatibility, and release-policy commitments that documentation review alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Sponsor a narrower shared-core v1
options.body: Approve locale resolution, stable message descriptors, English fallback, and compatibility rules now, while keeping coverage gates advisory until language and surface owners are committed.

options.title: Accept the full product contract
options.body: Approve the complete 22-locale coverage model, metadata extensions, storage ownership, and eventual blocking gates as the target architecture.

options.title: Retain surface-owned localization
options.body: Keep localization within existing UI, native, documentation, and adapter pipelines and rework or close the shared-runtime proposal.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrower shared-core v1
recommendation.body: Approve locale resolution, stable message descriptors, English fallback, and compatibility rules now, while keeping coverage gates advisory until language and surface owners are committed.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the clearest prior owner-level direction on OpenClaw localization architecture and are the best available router for renewed product alignment.
